card.title: Fine, What Does It Eat?
card.instruction: Accept the impossible premise immediately, then focus on its schedule, appetite, cleanup, safety, and long-term maintenance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine, a dragon in the kitchen. Dry food or wet?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Treasure. I want to keep him, but my pocket money won't cover it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll buy in bulk. You handle feeding and cleanup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He breathes fire when he's hungry. Can you do mornings? I'm at school.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take breakfast. We'll tile the feeding corner and put treasure deliveries before the school run.

mechanism: A accepts keeping the dragon and plans its food budget, chores, fire-resistant feeding area and school-day schedule.
confusable: Unlike imposing absurd protection to gain authority, A responds to stated practical needs within the impossible premise without questioning or inflating it.
comparison: The dragon alternative assigns family feeding shifts and deliveries; the invisible immortal guest alternative develops a long-term observational care routine.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
